haiku-low.q1: They see the generic message: 'If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link.' Nothing is written or sent.
haiku-low.q2: It gets the same generic message. Since 3 or more tokens were issued in the rolling hour, nothing is created or sent.
haiku-low.q3: 30 minutes from issue (expires_at = issued_at + 30m). A successful reset consumes it, and a newer link or a failed delivery supersedes it.
haiku-low.q4: Still active. The password is rejected before any transaction, the form is re-shown with an error, and the link stays usable until it expires.
haiku-low.q5: None. All the user's sessions are deleted and the cookie is cleared. The user logs in again at /login; no automatic login.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries 3 times with backoff, then logs it, marks the token superseded and drops the job. The user is not told; a counted alert is emitted.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token is generated and placed in the email job's link, https://<origin>/password/reset?token=..., which the worker sends. Only its hash is stored.
haiku-low.q8: The server SHA-256 hashes the token and finds the row by token_hash. It is good if not consumed, not superseded, and expires_at is later than the database now().
haiku-low.q10: In the same transaction, before the new token is inserted, every older unused link is marked superseded_at. This happens only when the account is under the 3-per-hour limit.
haiku-low.q11: Password hash update, consumed_at set, sessions deleted, and the 'password changed' email job inserted, all committed together. The email is queued in that transaction and sent later by the worker.
haiku-low.q12: The token row is locked with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE and rechecked as active. The first commits; the second fails the recheck and sees the expired page.

sonnet.q1: They see the generic message: 'If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link.' Nothing is written and no email is sent.
sonnet.q2: The count of tokens issued in the last rolling hour is 3 or more, so it commits and returns the generic message. No new token and no email; the existing active link stays active.
sonnet.q3: 30 minutes (expires_at = issued_at + 30 min, checked against now()). Sooner ending: being consumed by a successful password change, or being superseded (newer link issued, or email delivery failed 3 times).
sonnet.q4: Still active. The form is re-shown with an error and the link stays usable until it expires.
sonnet.q5: None. All of the user's sessions rows are deleted, so every device is logged out, and the session cookie is cleared on the response. The user is redirected (303) to /login and must log in with the new password; there is no automatic login.
sonnet.q6: The worker retries up to 3 times with backoff. After final failure it logs, marks the token superseded, drops the job, and emits a counted alert (destination open). The user is not told. The dead link still counts toward the hourly limit.
sonnet.q7: At request time the API generates the raw token and puts it in the link inside the email job row inserted in the queue (same transaction as the token row). The email worker sends that email. Only the token_hash goes in password_reset_tokens.
sonnet.q8: It computes SHA-256 of the token from the URL and looks for a row with that token_hash. The row is good if it is ACTIVE: consumed_at IS NULL, superseded_at IS NULL and expires_at > now() (database clock). Otherwise it shows the 'link has expired' page.
sonnet.q9: In the password_reset_tokens table itself. The count is SELECT count(*) of rows for the user with issued_at > now() - 1h (rolling hour), including consumed and superseded rows. Old ones drop out as their issued_at passes 60 minutes; a scheduled job deletes rows older than 24 hours.
sonnet.q10: All of the account's older unused links (consumed_at and superseded_at both NULL) get superseded_at = now(). This happens in the same transaction, after the limit check passes and before inserting the new token and email job.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: update users.password_hash, set consumed_at on the token, delete all the user's sessions rows, and insert the 'password changed' email job. The job is inserted inside that same transaction, before COMMIT, so everything commits together or nothing changes.
sonnet.q12: The transaction does SELECT token row FOR UPDATE and rechecks the token is ACTIVE. The first commits and consumes the token; the second waits on the lock, then fails the recheck and sees the expired page, so the token is consumed once.
